figures.caption: Fig. 2 EEGJev-Bench. a, We checked the public EEG releases against their original datasets and corrected discrepancies when building the benchmark. Within each scored source, training and test windows come from different participants. Each question pairs one or two EEG windows with a prompt and answer choices. D1–D4 and T1 use windows of 1, 2 or 4 s. b, D1 asks about one attribute. D2 asks two questions about the same window, chosen so that knowing one answer does not reveal the other. D3 asks the model to select an ordered category, such as an age group. D4 tests refusal by removing the correct option. A matched, answerable version removes one incorrect option. D1h repeats each D1 test question using two phrasings absent from training. c, T1 asks which of two windows shows a given label. T2 asks whether an event occurs in the first or second half of an 8, 16 or 30 s window. The D3 example uses the Dortmund age bins. The highlighted bin illustrates one possible answer. The other five examples come from the asym validation set.

Fig. 3 Question following, text controls and transfer to held-out tasks. a, Two questions about familiar attributes share an EEG window and an ordered list of options. The left column counts a label as correct when it belongs to the requested attribute. EEGJev scores average three training seeds for each of 13 test sources (380,570 eligible questions per seed). The last row weights sources equally. b, Changes are relative to scores with the original D1 questions and options. Whiskers show paired 95% intervals from resampling tasks within sources. Letter codes replace the candidate text. The test set covers 109 tasks from 17 sources. c,d, Bars show means across three training seeds.

Table 1 D1 source-balanced mean balanced accuracy (%), seed means, each model over the tasks it covers. Differences to EEGNet are paired over the Tasks column on common rows, with 95% intervals from a bootstrap over tasks within sources. LaBraM has no models for chbmit, hbn and sleep, NeuroLM no input for hbn and sleep, and LEAF no predictions for chbmit, deprest, hbn, mom and sleep. The averaged row uses the rule described in “Inference rules for known tasks and ordered-bin scores”. Validation is used for model selection where applicable. Shading shows BA on all 109 tasks. Bold marks the highest BA within each split.

Fig. 4 Model comparisons across EEGJev-Bench. Each pair of bars compares EEGJev with the named baseline on the test tasks that both cover. The Tasks column gives this count. Scores weight sources equally. d, The upper rows compare EEGJev’s trained refusal head with confidence thresholds. The lower rows apply the full-label check to both models. e,f, Fixed rules combine D1 outputs. The lower rows in f use time-ordered readouts trained on the same T2 labels as EEGJev.

Fig. 5 Paired questions, ordered bins and refusal. a, Dark and light bars show balanced accuracy per question and joint accuracy, respectively. The joint score balances across observed answer combinations. Each model is scored on the tasks it covers. Ordinary denotes the ordinary classification head, and fused denotes its equal-weight combination with EEGJev. PS denotes a per-source model. b, Each open circle is one of 59 matched tasks. Bars show source means and the equally weighted mean over ten sources. c, Colour bars and values show the balanced accuracy of the shared EEGJev D3 branch on 22 tasks by window length. Dashes mark unavailable tasks. d, Mean absolute bin error for models covering all 22 tasks. e, The score averages the rate of refusing when no option fits and the rate of answering when a correct option is present. The full-label check also scores every known class. f, Matched differences between the shared refusal head and the listed confidence rules. The right column gives each comparison’s task count. Whiskers in b,f give paired 95% intervals from 10,000 resamples of tasks within sources, conditional on the evaluated participants. The scores are from the test split.

Fig. 6 Temporal decisions across questions and sources. a,b, Bars give source-balanced accuracy on matched T1 and T2 tasks, respectively. Each dot shows the difference between EEGJev and the EEGNet rule on one task. EEGJev trained on temporal labels. The fixed rules compare D1 scores between windows for T1 and combine successive one-second D1 predictions for T2. c, EEGJev and both readouts trained on the same T2 labels. The readouts use time-ordered one-second class probabilities. Bars show paired source-balanced differences averaged across three seeds on 15 test tasks from seven sources and 37 participants. Whiskers give 95% intervals from 10,000 paired resamples of participants within fixed sources, or of sources and participants. d, Signed differences between EEGJev and the fixed EEGNet rule by source and duration. Dashes mark unavailable comparisons. PHOTO has direct scores for two durations. e,f, Paired differences between shared EEGJev and other models on T1 and T2, respectively. Whiskers give 95% intervals from 10,000 paired resamples of tasks within sources. Counts give the number of matched tasks in each comparison. The comparisons use fixed compositions except for the per-source direct head, which also trained on temporal labels.
